title: Bounded Unreal widget inspection and text hiding
excerpt: Bounded Unreal widget inspection and text hiding MCP server 0.3.3 and Unreal bridge 0.2.9 extend existing Blueprint inspection with the Widget Blueprint designer tree and editor bindings. Inspection reports at most 256
html:
Bounded Unreal widget inspection and text hiding

MCP server 0.3.3 and Unreal bridge 0.2.9 extend existing Blueprint inspection with the Widget Blueprint designer tree and editor bindings. Inspection reports at most 256 widgets and 512 bindings; it does not report live viewport instances or inherited trees. Text fields include template text, font size and automatic wrapping.

Existing Blueprint edit recipes accept an optional widgets array, with at most 32 exact-name hide_text operations. The native operation accepts only existing TextBlocks, collapses the selected field and removes its Visibility binding so that the binding cannot immediately override the change. Text bindings and other fields are preserved. No widget is deleted and no existing asset is saved automatically. Visibility and complete editor-binding recovery are included in stale-preview fingerprints and rollback snapshots. Oversized mutation snapshots are rejected. Graph-only payloads omit the empty array for compatibility with older bridges.

Validation: 303 Python tests and Ruff passed. The UE 5.6.1 Editor target completed DLL linking and target metadata generation. Both native automation tests passed in a disposable host: exact-text hiding and visibility-binding recovery, and oversized-tree mutation rejection. The first commandlet launch in ForgeMCPDev failed at Editor startup with a SharedPointer assertion before running tests; the isolated host completed with exit code 0. Evidence is in Saved/WidgetBridge029/ and Saved/WidgetNativeTests029/.

The tested plugin was installed into OnTheGoNav after the user saved and closed Unreal. The installer backed up the previous plugin and project descriptor. The reopened session [session id redacted] confirmed the correct project, and the loaded DLL path and SHA-256 matched the tested build: F71803794AB2391F523ADAD9182028F4A1F7856275813B16CBE922681C8A2470.

Live inspection of /Game/OnTheGoNAV/OnTheGoNAV found seven template widgets and 11 bindings. Its two TextBlocks are DistanceText and Location; the latter reads the component's Nav Text, while the former binds to the distance function. There is no second distance field in this template. No hide_text mutation was applied to it. During the user-operated Play run, actor enumeration listed ten planet destinations. Detailed actor/component inspection is currently blocked during PIE. Overlapping marker instances remain a hypothesis requiring isolation and visual confirmation.

The isolation test temporarily set only the loaded BP_Planet_1 navigation component's DistanceTextVisible from true to false through reviewed native component preview/apply. The user then ran Play and confirmed one distance line remained. This establishes that the two observed lines belong to separate markers, rather than two text fields in one widget. After Play stopped, a second reviewed edit restored true and a fresh inspection verified it. Neither diagnostic edit saved the level. The permanent display treatment is awaiting the user's preference; the duplicate-line repair is not yet complete.
